clue.text: Shakespearean character put to death by hanging

definitions.text: Shakespearean character put to death by hanging

parts.words: Shakespearean character put to death by hanging
parts.note: the hanging is not a noose but a wall tapestry, the arras through which Hamlet stabs the eavesdropping old counsellor

explanation.surface: A figure from Shakespeare who meets his end on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests execution by rope; here it is a hanging cloth, the arras behind which the courtier hides in Hamlet and is run through.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chamberlain in Hamlet dies when the prince stabs through a tapestry hanging he is hiding behind.

clue.text: What could be composed by pestilent snooper?

definitions.text: What could be composed by pestilent snooper?

indicators.note: composed signals the letters of the two words are put together anew

explanation.surface: Wondering what a nasty prying busybody might write.
explanation.walkthrough: All sixteen letters of 'pestilent snooper' are rearranged, and such a person would indeed write malicious anonymous mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful anonymous letters are the kind of thing a malicious busybody would send.

clue.text: See 1
What one must have observed rising round start of day

indicators.note: round says the reversed word goes about the letter that follows
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: seen means observed

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Something one must have spotted coming up around daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN reversed is NEES, which wraps round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessities are things a person must have.

clue.text: Media company formed from A T T industries

indicators.note: formed from says the answer is made by reworking the letters given

explanation.surface: A media business created out of the AT&T industries.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters A, T, T and INDUSTRIES are rearranged. AT&T is the American telecoms giant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood film studio founded by Chaplin, Pickford, Fairbanks and Griffith.

clue.text: Part of flower, it's in rim, set back

indicators.note: set back means the assembled letters are turned round to run the other way
in says the letters of it's sit within the word for rim

parts.note: the lip of a cup or jug is its rim
the letters of it's, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that part of a flower sits recessed inside its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set back' turns LITSIP round; 'rim' is the edge of a cup, not of the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The female seed-bearing organ at a bloom's centre, made up of stigma, style and ovary.

clue.text: Industrious type that's playing well on grass

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a player on good form is in form
the ant is proverbially hard-working

explanation.surface: A hardworking sort performs well on the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a playing surface; it is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for telling the police, so a grass is a police tip-off source.

clue.text: Drive in explosive weapon

indicators.note: in places the driving word inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT, trinitrotoluene
to ride is to drive along, travel

explanation.surface: Push an explosive device into the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive weapon' reads as one phrase, but the explosive only wraps the drive; the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-pronged spear, and also the name of a submarine-launched missile.

clue.text: Belgian city, historically superior

definitions.meaning: the French-speaking city on the Meuse in eastern Belgium
in feudal times, the lord to whom a vassal owed service

explanation.definitionFit: A Walloon city on the Meuse; and a feudal lord, the superior of vassals.

clue.text: Incarcerated frequently, I am near end of sentence, almost too late

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison, so being locked up is being in the nick
oft is the old poetic word for often
contracted to I'm

indicators.note: end of picks out the closing letter of the word sentence

explanation.surface: A frequent jailbird nearing the end of a prison term reflects that it all came a bit late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' and 'incarcerated' paint a prison scene; the sentence only lends its last letter. 'Near' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the last possible moment, just before it would have been too late.

clue.text: Restore harmony after conflict — fool showing up in nice warpaint

indicators.note: in places the reversed fool inside the word for nice

parts.note: kind means nice

indicators.note: in a down clue showing up means the word reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: an ass is a fool
jocular term for cosmetics

explanation.surface: An idiot turns up wearing pleasant make-up to patch things up after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: ASS reversed gives SSA, set in KIND to make KISSAND. Warpaint is humorous slang for a woman's cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for ending a quarrel and becoming friends again.

clue.text: Foremen, Irish, interrupting lots of deliveries

indicators.note: interrupting means the word for Irish breaks into the cricket term

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so overs are lots of deliveries
Erse is an old name for the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Irish bosses keep breaking into a busy schedule of deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels or post, but these are cricket balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervisors of workers, like foremen on a site or shop floor.

clue.text: Contributor to Chaucer and to Shakespeare even

indicators.note: to here means belonging to, so the letters are part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone who wrote for both Chaucer and Shakespeare, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Shakespeare' and the start of 'even'. The pilgrim tells a tale in The Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Canterbury pilgrims, a manor steward, tells his own tale, so he contributes to Chaucer's collection.

clue.text: Sets sitting positions

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to set a puzzle or question is to put it forward
attitudes a model holds while sitting for an artist or photographer

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to put forward a problem, and the stances held for a portrait.

clue.text: Most dependable form of aid in set variations

indicators.note: in places the reworked aid inside the varied sets

parts.note: two rearrangements of the word set, one placed before the other

indicators.note: form of signals the letters of aid are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most reliable form of aid comes in various kits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' makes ADI; 'set variations' are two rearrangements of the one word, placed either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of steady, meaning most reliable or stable.

clue.text: An experimental flower, pure white

parts.note: an gives A
lab, the laboratory, as in lab-grown or lab test
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A trial bloom that comes out pure white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is not the definition here; it supplies the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth fine-grained gypsum stone, used to describe skin or surfaces of translucent whiteness.

clue.text: Person taxed ere a party gets thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out signals the letters of the three words are scattered

explanation.surface: A taxpayer is ejected before a party gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ERE A PARTY are rearranged. Rates were a British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who paid rates, the old British local tax on property.

clue.text: Was feeding, tucked into sickly sundae — could become this

definitions.text: Was feeding, tucked into sickly sundae — could become this

indicators.note: tucked into puts the eating word inside the shuffled dessert letters
sickly signals the letters of the dessert are disordered

parts.note: past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Someone who has been gorging on a cloying ice-cream dish may end up feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sickly' makes NAUSED, and the whole clue describes what overeating such a pudding leads to.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sick to the stomach is the likely result of eating too much of a cloying pudding.

clue.text: One taking most interest capturing Prince, one who's seized the throne

indicators.note: capturing means the lender holds the letter for prince inside

parts.note: a usurer lends money at excessive interest

explanation.surface: A greedy lender kidnaps a prince and grabs the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most interest' is excessive interest on a loan, not the greatest curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who seizes power, especially a crown, without right.

clue.text: Give medical care special favour

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to attend to a patient or illness
as a noun, a delight or indulgence given to someone

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor attends to patients; a gift or outing is an indulgence.

clue.text: Serious art being rewarded?

definitions.meaning: in old English thou art paid becomes thou ..., the second-person form of the verb to earn

explanation.definitionFit: Sincere and solemn; and the archaic second-person form of a verb meaning to be paid.

clue.text: Beat poet

explanation.definitionFit: To hammer hard; and the surname of the American author of The Cantos.

clue.text: Newspapers subject to coercion

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to pressure or force someone

explanation.definitionFit: The journalistic media; and to urge or force someone.

clue.text: Blade of plough about right to work in farm in US

parts.note: the ploughshare is the cutting blade, often just the share
c, short for circa, means about
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Farm tips: turn the plough blade about to the right before working American fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' gives OP, the abbreviated opus. The definition is American: tenants farm land for a share of the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenant farming in the US South, paying the landlord with part of the harvest.

clue.text: Like essayist's vigorous style one's taken to heart

indicators.note: taken to heart puts the letter for one into the middle of the style word

parts.note: elan is dash or vigour
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is is

explanation.surface: An essayist's punchy style is taken to heart by readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the pen name used by Charles Lamb for his Essays.

clue.text: Fast conveyance to state ball

parts.note: to state is to express
in cricket a ball bowled is a delivery

explanation.surface: Quick transport is laid on to take guests to a state ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State ball' looks like a grand dance; it is a verb and a cricket ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium courier or postal service sending goods quickly.

clue.text: Guarantee something will be done for a certain property

definitions.meaning: a bond or pledge, or the person who stands as guarantor
the quality of being certain, certainty

explanation.definitionFit: A pledge or guarantor; and, in older usage, sureness itself.

clue.text: Plays record three times in combination an old single?

parts.note: a DJ spins a disc
ter is Latin for three times, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A DJ spins one record three times over, an old single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old single' sounds like a vintage record; it is an unmarried older woman. TER is the prescription Latin for thrice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for an unmarried woman, especially one past the usual age of marriage.
